methodology.purpose: Qualitative matchup, injury, role and volume context for the exact Stage 1 qualifiers; no prop selection.
methodology.evidence_policy: Distinguish sourced facts from inference; do not equate team defense rank or fantasy points allowed with direct player-market allowance.
methodology.market_reference: Use updated Stage 1 DraftKings snapshot lines only; snapshot not independently verified live.

game_context.pace_and_game_environment: Matchup model source estimates 42.5 total points and Giants 22.5 implied points; secondary projection, not DraftKings quote.
injuries: NFL official Week 10 injury report lists Cam Skattebo and J.J. McCarthy full participation and no game designation.
Jayden Daniels full participation; Lucas Patrick ruled out.
Treylon Burks has no game designation after Wednesday DNP; final report says Wednesday was planned rest after Tuesday work.
Chig Okonkwo full participation Tuesday and Wednesday.
Malik Nabers, Darnell Mooney and Theo Johnson full participation.

assessments.supporting_evidence: NFL official Week 10 report lists full participation; Washington had 207.1 passing yards/game through Week 9.
assessments.contrary_evidence: NYG ranked 3rd in passing yards allowed (177.8/game); Washington center Lucas Patrick ruled out.
assessments.interpretation: Availability is positive, but a strong pass defense and center change add downside.

assessments.supporting_evidence: NFL official report lists full participation and no game designation; Giants RB snap share through Week 9 was 55%, vs Singletary 45%.
assessments.contrary_evidence: Returning from hamstring issue after missing Week 9; usage on return remains uncertain. DraftKings line now 52.5, with L10 Market HR 8/10.
assessments.interpretation: Role/availability is encouraging, and historical rate supports the line, but immediate post-injury workload remains the key variable.

assessments.supporting_evidence: Was the other part of Giants' backfield rotation; 45% season snap share through Week 9.
assessments.contrary_evidence: Skattebo is cleared and had 55% season snap share; split remains competitive.
assessments.interpretation: The returning Skattebo reduces confidence in Singletary's share of carries.

assessments.supporting_evidence: Commanders usage report identifies White as lead back through Week 9: 54 carries, 46% offensive snap share.
assessments.contrary_evidence: Week 9 report describes near-even White/Ekeler playing-time split; NYG is a top-five total defense, but its rush-defense rank differs from pass defense.
assessments.interpretation: Role is meaningful, but carry competition and overall defensive quality temper the rushing matchup.

assessments.supporting_evidence: 78 targets, 53 catches, 648 yards; 33% Giants target share and 35% air-yard share through Week 9; full practice.
assessments.contrary_evidence: NYG faces a Washington defense ranked 20th in total yards allowed, but no receiver-specific coverage metric was verified.
assessments.interpretation: High target concentration and full availability support opportunity.

assessments.supporting_evidence: 78 targets/53 catches; 33% team target share; full participation on official injury report.
assessments.contrary_evidence: No verified player-specific catch matchup metric; team defense ranking is broad.
assessments.interpretation: Consistent target volume is a strong base for receptions.

assessments.supporting_evidence: Full participation; 26 targets, 12 catches, 167 yards through Week 9.
assessments.contrary_evidence: Approximately 9% Giants target share; behind Nabers, Likely and Fields in the reported distribution.
assessments.interpretation: Availability is positive but the season opportunity is limited.

assessments.supporting_evidence: Full practice and 12 catches on 26 targets through Week 9.
assessments.contrary_evidence: Only 26 targets in the Giants' season sample; multiple teammates have larger target roles.
assessments.interpretation: Catch line is low but target volume is not especially secure.

assessments.supporting_evidence: 49 targets, 30 catches, 303 yards; leads Commanders in targets. Full participation not required by injury report.
assessments.contrary_evidence: Recent three-game target share down 3 percentage points; 14.7% Week 9 share was season low; NYG top-five total defense.
assessments.interpretation: Still a leading option, but recent target trend and quality of opponent are concerns.

assessments.supporting_evidence: 49 targets and 30 catches through Week 9; team-leading target total.
assessments.contrary_evidence: Recent target share down 3 points and Week 9 season-low 14.7%.
assessments.interpretation: Volume history is useful, but current trend is less favorable.

assessments.supporting_evidence: 22 targets, 12 catches, 233 yards through Week 9; target share has increased 13.1 percentage points in last three games vs earlier sample. Final report: no game designation.
assessments.contrary_evidence: Missed prior game with foot injury and did not practice Wednesday; final report indicates planned rest/no designation.
assessments.interpretation: Recent role growth is positive, but injury interruption and only 22 season targets remain relevant.

assessments.supporting_evidence: Week 9: 5 catches on 7 targets for 58 yards; 57% route share while Burks was absent.
assessments.contrary_evidence: Only 8 targets and 5 catches across season; Week 9 accounts for nearly all targets in the dataset; Burks returned.
assessments.interpretation: Low line and recent game are positive, but one-game spike may not persist.

assessments.supporting_evidence: Week 9: 5 receptions on 7 targets, 57% route share.
assessments.contrary_evidence: Only 8 season targets total through Week 9; target volume highly concentrated in one game; Burks returns.
assessments.interpretation: Recent performance supports the low threshold, but sample and role stability are weak.

assessments.supporting_evidence: 69 targets, 46 catches, 448 yards through Week 9; 75% snap share; third-most fantasy points allowed to TEs by Washington in matchup source.
assessments.contrary_evidence: Target share over latest three games is 22%, down 5 percentage points from earlier games.
assessments.interpretation: Strong season-long involvement and favorable positional matchup, with recent target share cooling.

assessments.supporting_evidence: 69 targets and 46 catches; 75% snap share through Week 9.
assessments.contrary_evidence: Latest-three-game target share is down 5 points; no direct catches-allowed data used.
assessments.interpretation: High season-long involvement supports catch opportunity, though trend has softened.

assessments.supporting_evidence: Full participation and no game designation on NFL report.
assessments.contrary_evidence: Giants target distribution is led by Nabers and Likely; no reliable target-volume figure for Johnson was retrieved.
assessments.interpretation: Health is not the issue; opportunity evidence is insufficient relative to the leading pass catchers.

assessments.supporting_evidence: Full participation and no game designation.
assessments.contrary_evidence: No reliable target volume or route-share figure verified; Likely is the established lead receiving TE.
assessments.interpretation: Limited evidence of a stable catch workload.

assessments.supporting_evidence: 31 targets, 23 catches, 238 yards through Week 9; latest-three-game target share 19%, up 6 points; full participation Tuesday and Wednesday.
assessments.contrary_evidence: Giants rank 3rd in pass defense by pass yards allowed; only 8 Commanders games in sample.
assessments.interpretation: Recent role trend and playing time support catches, but opposing defense is strong.

caveats: Usage statistics are third-party compiled through Week 9; official box scores are the underlying basis where noted.
Cam Skattebo has no injury designation in the NFL official report, but returning after hamstring injury creates workload uncertainty.
Van Jefferson's Week 9 target spike is a one-game sample and coincided with Burks' absence.
Team defense rankings are not player-specific coverage metrics.
Fantasy points allowed to tight ends is not directly equivalent to receiving yards or receptions allowed.
DraftKings odds remain the Stage 1 repository snapshot and are not live-verified.
